learning_objective: 🎯 Explore more exciting career skills! Discover the art and science behind Food Processing, Baking, and creating beautiful Handicrafts.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Turning raw agricultural products into consumable food. For example, changing raw wheat into flour, or turning fresh tomatoes into ketchup. It adds value to the crop.
Treating food so that it does not get spoiled by bacteria or fungi. Making pickles (using oil/salt), jams (using sugar), or freezing peas extends their 'shelf-life'.
Baking is both a science and an art. It involves using dry heat in an oven to make bread, cakes, and cookies. Exact measurements of flour, sugar, and yeast are critical!
Making decorative or useful items entirely by hand or using simple tools. This includes pottery (clay work), basket weaving, and traditional embroidery.
These vocations are perfect for starting small businesses from home. You can bake cakes for birthdays or sell homemade organic jams to your community!

fun_activity.title: 🫙 The Preservation Test
fun_activity.instructions: Take two slices of apple. Put one in a bowl with a lot of salt or sugar (preservatives), and leave the other slice plain on a plate. Check them after 2 days. The plain one will rot, but the preserved one won't!

exam_tips: 📌 Know the difference between Processing (changing form) and Preservation (preventing decay).
📌 Salt, sugar, oil, and vinegar are natural food preservatives.
📌 Baking relies heavily on exact mathematical ratios—too much baking powder can ruin a cake!
quick_recap: ⭐ Food processing helps farmers earn more money by selling 'value-added' products.
⭐ Handicrafts preserve the rich culture and traditional skills of a region.
⭐ Hygiene and cleanliness are the most important rules in any food-related vocation.
